text:
marcus: Heads-up — MerchantOne is asking for a tight migration POC. They want a drop-in that preserves prompt/response parity and keeps token billing within a 12% delta. Can we outline constraints and blockers?

anna (SE): Great, I'm on it. Primary asks: 1) identical input/response shape for adapter 2) deterministic sampling for A/B 3) a fallback path that preserves SLA.

teju (security): Also they need answers for the security questionnaire: KMS integration, data residency, and an on-prem option. I flagged the SOC2 controls section for legal.

elain (eng): Quick note — our compat shim can map endpoints 1:1, but we need to call out differences in system tokens when using competitor header X-Client-ID. We'll convert to 'x-redwood-client'. Example mapping they asked for: ```POST /v1/generate -> POST /v1/responses model: {"alias":"gpt-x"} input: raw prompt```

sam (solutions): For parity tests we should run a 1000 prompt corpus and 200 randomized prompts with temperature=0 and temperature=0.7. Compare tokens, latency p95, and top-1 answer BLEU/ROUGE-ish checks.

marcus: Pricing question — MerchantOne is worried about token billing changes. Can we show a sample invoice delta? They want a worst-case model switch scenario.

anna (SE): I'll produce a delta table. We can simulate tokenization differences locally: tokenizer mismatch can add 5-10% tokens alone. If we enable prefix caching and batching, net token cost often drops.

teju (security): On questionnaire: they require KMS + HSM mention, key rotation policy, and proof we never persist raw prompts in logs for PII flows. We can provide the private deployment whitepaper page and a screenshot of audit logs retention policy.

elaine (eng): Technical blocker — competitor supports streaming with chunked JSON objects; our runtime streams SSE by default. We can offer a compatibility proxy that re-chunks SSE -> chunked-json, but it's an engineering spike. ETA ~ 3 days for a minimal shim.

sam (solutions): Also note their integration uses session affinity (sticky sessions) for KV cache. We need guidance: either offer sticky-router config on Dedicated or document how to warm KV on our side. Leads to an acceptance criteria item: "no increase in 500/timeout errors during warmup window."

marcus: Can we commit to a canary rollback plan if results diverge? Client wants automatic fallback to competitor at 0.5% error delta.

elaine (eng): We can wire a policy: route primary -> redwood, fallback -> origin-competitor. Need legal ok to proxy traffic to competitor. Also need routing key in header to signal fallback reason.

teju (security): Legal will want a data flow diagram for that. Proxying back to competitor may be a no-go for some regs; flagging as enterprise blocker.

anna (SE): Next steps: I'll scope POC runbook. Items: mapping shim repo link, 1k prompt corpus, cost delta sim, security questionnaire answers, fallback routing design, acceptance test scripts.

deploy-bot: deploy/compat-shim-spike queued by elaine — builds: #3712 status: pending

sam (solutions): For acceptance tests, add prompt parity threshold: >= 92% semantic match on control set and token delta <= 15%. If either fails, we keep canary at 1% and require manual signoff.

marcus: Perfect. Anna, can you draft timeline for the customer by EOD? Include the 3-day shim spike and a 2-week POC run with daily health checks.

anna (SE): Yes — will send a short deck and runbook. I'll ping legal for the proxy question and teju for the questionnaire artifacts.

teju (security): I'll prepare the KMS + audit screenshots and a paragraph on rotation/keys. Also adding a note on in-transit encryption and HSM options for Private.

elaine (eng): If legal greenlights proxying, I'll start the shim today. Otherwise we'll present guidance for hybrid warmup and longer canary.

marcus: Thanks team. I'll put together the pricing sketch and a short risk register for MerchantOne.

sam (solutions): I'll prepare the 1k prompt corpus — pulling from merchant domain samples and generic fuzz set. Will post in the drive.

anna (SE): Filing a follow-up thread with the one-pager and timeline once I have legal's answer. :thumbsup:

marcus: Closing notes — keep replies short here. If you need me to join a call with the client tomorrow, say so.

elaine (eng): I can join the call if it's technical deep-dive.

teju (security): Same for questionnaire review.

sam (solutions): Happy to run through the acceptance tests on the call.

marcus: Cool — thanks everyone.
